children: Bentley, the luxury-car brand owned by Volkswagen
, has launched its first fully electric vehicle, the Torcal SUV, as it seeks to move into the EV market while retaining elements of its traditional brand identity.
The Torcal starts at £173,000 ($230,000), putting it toward the lower end of Bentley’s
lineup. Its design retains features associated with the automaker’s combustion-engine models, including diamond-shaped headlights intended to evoke a conventional grille.
has also incorporated an orchestral soundtrack using timpani and smaller drums to reproduce the sound and feel associated with a V8 engine.
“Our intention was always to make a Bentley
first,” Chief Executive Officer Frank-Steffen Walliser told Reuters. “We feel people are not asking for a completely different car just because it's electric.”

has shown the SUV to existing and prospective customers, with interest coming from Europe, the Middle East, and US states with high EV adoption. About half of the interest is from existing customers, while the rest comes from people new to the brand, he said.

has invested £350 million in its Crewe, northwest England, plant to produce the Torcal. The company had previously delayed its first EV until 2026 and dropped a goal of becoming fully electric by 2030, saying customers were not ready for the transition.
The Torcal’s launch campaign in China is scheduled to begin next year.

title: Bentley launches Torcal as its first fully electric model
